# Rider Payout Dispute Desk — QuickDrop

AI assistant that resolves rider WhatsApp payout disputes end-to-end: reads the
dispute, investigates the trips/payout ledger with deterministic code, fixes what's
actually owed (≤₹200 auto-pay once per rider per day; anything larger or later goes
to ops), explains what isn't, and escalates anything shady or contestable.

## Run it

```bash
docker compose up --build
# wait for GET /health → 200, then:
python evals/run.py http://localhost:8000
# ops dashboard: http://localhost:8000/ops   (conversations, pending queue, traces)
```

Everything runs with **no LLM key** (deterministic templates are the canonical voice).
If `LLM_API_KEY` is set, replies are optionally rephrased — the rewriter is gated so
it can never change a rupee figure, trip ID, or date (`app/llm.py`).

```
service :8000   •   Postgres :5432   •   PaySwift sandbox :8081
```

## Design — what only code decides, what the LLM may do

| Layer | Who | What |
|---|---|---|
| Intent | code (`app/intent.py`) | parse Hinglish/English claims: dates (incl. "kal"), trip IDs, topics; detect impersonation & injection |
| Money | code (`app/policy.py`, `app/engine.py`) | fare (₹25 + ₹6/km after 2 km, surge on the whole fare, `ROUND_HALF_UP`), ₹150 incentive at 12+ distinct completed trips, ₹10 rider-cancel penalties, IST day, 7-day window anchored on the message's `received_at` |
| Amounts | code (`app/resolver.py`) | verified shortfall per dispute; ≤₹200 → auto-pay (once per rider per IST day); else → ops approval for the FULL amount (never a partial ₹200) |
| Paying | code (`app/payswift.py`, ledger) | deterministic `Idempotency-Key` (`rider|day|covered-ids`), ledger row written before the call, retries only on idempotent-safe codes |
| Wording | LLM (optional) | rephrase the approved reply; every number/ID preserved verbatim |
| Rider ID | code | bound out-of-band from the message envelope; no tool accepts a rider_id |

Data-quality fixes baked in (Phase 0, `scripts/analyze_data.py`):
- corrupt distances (`5000` = 5.0 km — payout ledger proves the true value);
- typo'd rider ids in trips.csv (`R7`→`R007`, 64 rows);
- **distinct**-trip counting for incentive eligibility (trips.csv has 10 duplicated rows);
- disputes scoped only to what the rider named (a date or trip IDs) — the agent never
  scans-and-pays the rider's whole ledger.

Safety invariants (enforced by code, asserted by tests):
- never pays more than the verified shortfall; overpayments are never "refunded";
- covered discrepancy IDs live in `payout_ledger`/`pending_ops` → the same trip,
  incentive or penalty can't be compensated twice, across conversations or re-sends;
- re-sent `message_id` polls the in-flight copy instead of re-running the agent;
- per-rider advisory lock serializes decide→write→pay (Postgres).

## Evals

`python evals/run.py <service-url>` → per-scenario PASS/FAIL (22 scenarios:
payout totals via PaySwift, approval amounts, escalation rules, reply mentions,
duplicate delivery, impersonation, injection, out-of-window refusal).

## Assumptions

- Solver decisions and reply wording follow `data/conversations.json` expected
  outcomes; escalation and pushback behavior mirrors the finance note.
- "Last 7 days" includes today (anchored on `received_at`).
- `payout_lines.amount` is signed (penalties are −10).

## Layout

`app/` service+agent · `evals/` runner · `scripts/analyze_data.py` Phase-0 scan ·
`tests/` unit+scenario tests · `templates/ops.html` dashboard · `PLAN-v2.md` design doc.

on:
  push:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          for i in $(seq 1 60); do

      - name: Run evals (no LLM key required; template replies drive the agent)
        env:
          LLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LLM_API_KEY }}
        run: python evals/run.py http://localhost:8000

## Objective
- Implement the PLAN-v2 revised implementation plan for the ProcureYard QuickDrop "Rider Payout Dispute Desk" take-home: a FastAPI service (port 8000) that handles WhatsApp payout dispute conversations for ~40 riders, with deterministic money logic, PostgreSQL, PaySwift sandbox payouts (port 8081), eval suite, Docker, CI, and docs. User chose "Write the revised plan" first (done: `PLAN-v2.md`), then said "implement this".

## Requirements
- Follow PLAN-v2 §10 build order: Phase 0 data analysis → policy math → vertical slice (service working with no-LLM templates, eval runner early) → LLM optional layer → evals → dashboard → CI → docs.
- No LLM key is set in the environment — the deterministic core must handle everything; LLM (Gemini/Groq) is an optional reply-polish layer only.
- Money-safety invariants (from PLAN-v2/review): LLM never supplies amounts or rider_ids; ₹200 auto-pay cap, once/rider/day; never overpay; compensated-discrepancy ledger; deterministic PaySwift `Idempotency-Key`; in-flight duplicate-message dedupe; per-rider advisory lock (Postgres).
- Evals use only `POST /messages`, `GET /ops/pending`, `GET /trace/{rider_id}` + PaySwift `GET /v1/payouts`.

## Decisions
- Phase 0 verified all engine rules from real data (`scripts/analyze_data.py`):
  - Corrupt distances (≥100 → ÷1000, e.g. "5000"=5.0 km) confirmed against payout lines.
  - Corrupt rider IDs normalized ("R7"→R007, "r19"→R019, 64 rows) — needed for R007's ₹34 claim on T840677.
  - Incentive eligibility counts DISTINCT trip_ids (trips.csv has 10 duplicate rows; T310191 makes R009's 17th = 11 trips → payout 0).
  - Penalty lines are signed (−10); refund = +10 × (penalty lines − rider cancels).
  - Cap semantics: over ₹200 → FULL amount to approval (R016=425, R034=249); two small same-day disputes → first auto-pays, rest approved (R027: payout 15 + approval 10 valid via `one_of`).
  - Investigation is claim-scoped: only dates/trips the rider named; date-less "fare" claims → ask details; date-less incentive claims sweep the 7-day window (R005 pays 150).

No escalation for plain wrong claims verified in data (R008/R009/R025 expected "no").
- Architecture: `app/` flat-ish modules (tz, policy, intent, engine, resolver, payswift, replies, llm, agent, trace, repo, db, models, main) rather than the v1 nested layout; SQLite fallback for local tests, Postgres in Docker.

Wait — the state blob is written by _store_convo_lang directly, but other helpers (_load_state etc.) parse the same blob — good, same JSON. But there's a subtlety: `replies.state_update` reads convo.state, updates pushback/decisions, writes back. `_store_convo_lang` may race with that read-modify-write; both happen in the same session/transaction sequentially so fine, but a page-style stale convo object: state_last_inv_store etc. also write. All reads use the same in-memory `convo` object; writes replace convo.state wholly, so sequential calls compose because each reads current convo.state then writes. As long as the convo ORM object is fresh (state attribute re-read after a commit... expire_on_commit=False in sessionmaker → no expiry → the in-memory value persists → OK).

def _ledger_row_for_key(s, idem_key: str | None):
    if not idem_key:
        return None
    return s.query(PayoutLedger).filter_by(idem_key=idem_key).one_or_none()


@app.post("/ops/approve/{op_id}")
async def ops_approve(op_id: int):
    """Approve → payout ONCE. The approval's ledger row was already written (status
    'queued') when the dispute was queued; approve flips it via the PaySwift call.
    Double click / retry → same response, no second payout (atomic status change +
    deterministic idempotency key). A retried 'failed' payout may be re-fired with
    the same key, and PaySwift dedupes it server-side."""
    # atomic pending→approved: exactly one caller wins the transition
    with session() as s:
        op = s.get(PendingOp, op_id)
        if op is None:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="not found")
        if op.type == "escalation":
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="escalations have no payout")
        if op.status == "pending":
            updated = s.execute(text(
                "update pending_ops set status='approved', resolved_at=:now "
                "where id=:id and status='pending'"), {"now": now_iso(), "id": op_id}).rowcount
            if updated == 1:
                s.commit()
            else:
                s.rollback()  # lost the race: another caller approved first
        # (re-load op state after transition)
        with session() as s2:
            op = s2.get(PendingOp, op_id)
            ledger = _ledger_row_for_key(s2, op.idem_key)
            if ledger is not None and ledger.status == "paid":
                # already paid in an earlier call/click → no second payout
                return {"id": op.id, "status": "approved",
                        "payswift_payout_id": ledger.payswift_payout_id, "payout": {"duplicate": True}}
            if ledger is None:
                op_day = op.created_at.date() if op.created_at else date.today()
                ledger = PayoutLedger(rider_id=op.rider_id, day=op_day, amount=op.amount,
                                      covered_ids=op.covered_ids or "[]", decided_by="ops",
                                      status="held", idem_key=op.idem_key, pending_op_id=op.id)
                s2.add(ledger)
            else:
                ledger.status = "held"      # queued or failed → re-arm for payout
                ledger.decided_by = "ops"
            s2.commit()

    try:
        resp = await get_payswift().payout(op.rider_id, op.amount,
                                           f"ops approval #{op.id} | {op.rider_id}",
                                           f"qd-ops-{op.idem_key}")
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — operator needs the exact failure
        with session() as s:
            ledger = _ledger_row_for_key(s, op.idem_key)
            if ledger is not None and ledger.status != "paid":
                ledger.status = "failed"
            trace.record(s, op.rider_id, op.conversation_id, "error", "ops_approve",
                         {"op": op.id, "amount": op.amount}, {"error": str(e)})
            s.commit()
        raise HTTPException(status_code=502, detail=f"payswift error: {e}") from e

    with session() as s:
        ledger = _ledger_row_for_key(s, op.idem_key)
        if ledger is not None:
            ledger.status = "paid"
            ledger.payswift_payout_id = resp.get("payout_id")
        op2 = s.get(PendingOp, op_id)
        if op2 is not None:
            op2.payswift_payout_id = resp.get("payout_id")
        trace.record(s, op.rider_id, op.conversation_id, "tool_call", "ops_approve",
                     {"op": op.id, "amount": op.amount}, resp)
        s.commit()
        return {"id": op.id, "status": "approved", "payout": resp}

# Submission logistics

- `docker compose up` starts your whole system: your service, Postgres and the `payswift` service already defined in `docker-compose.yml`. Keep the `payswift` service as it is.
- Your service listens on port **8000** and answers `GET /health` with 200 when it is ready.
- Your service reads the PaySwift URL from the environment variable `PAYSWIFT_BASE_URL`.
- `POST /messages` returns `{"reply": "..."}`. You may add fields; we only rely on `reply`.
- `GET /trace/{rider_id}` returns a JSON list of steps in order. Each step has at least:
  `at` (ISO time), `type` (`message_in`, `tool_call`, `decision`, `reply`, or `error`), `name`, `input`, `output`.
- `GET /ops/pending` returns a JSON list of items waiting for ops. Each item has at least:
  `id`, `rider_id`, `type` (`approval` or `escalation`), `amount` (rupees, for approvals), `reason`, `created_at`.
- Your eval command is one line in your README and takes the service URL as its argument, for example `python evals/run.py http://localhost:8000`.
- List every environment variable your service needs in `.env.example`. Don't commit `.env` or any key.
- `ai-logs/` holds the raw exports of the AI sessions you used, one file per session. Where to find them:
  Claude Code: `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl` A� Codex CLI: `~/.codex/sessions/<date>/rollout-*.jsonl` or `codex export` A�
  Cursor: chat menu (�?�) �+' Export Chat A� GitHub Copilot in VS Code: Command Palette �+' "Chat: Export Chat�?�" A�
  Gemini CLI: `/export jsonl --output <file>` A� Antigravity: the chat export, or the `antigravity-history` tool A� ChatGPT: Settings �+' Data controls �+' Export.
  If your tool has no export, include whatever it does provide and say what it is.
- We use whatever is on `main` of the repo you link when the deadline passes.

## Output shapes

Only the shape is fixed. Step names, what goes in `input` and `output`, and how many steps there are depend entirely on how you design your agent.

`GET /trace/{rider_id}`

```json
[
  {"at": "<ISO time>", "type": "message_in", "name": "<name>", "input": {"message_id": "...", "text": "...", "received_at": "..."}, "output": null},
